description:
The End Times sequence is reviewed before the study turns to the new heavens and new earth. Wesam Saad revisits the relationship between creation, the cross, the church age, tribulation and the millennial kingdom within his premillennial framework. He connects the kingdom with promises to Israel and the subjection of Christ’s enemies, then follows the sequence through final judgment to the eternal state. Questions about competing interpretations focus on his commitment to the plain sense of prophetic promises while allowing for figures and types. His comparisons express the approach defended in this series rather than a neutral survey of every theological position.

The review also revisits the timing of the rapture, the role of angels, the Antichrist and the meaning of Christ’s victory over death. Saad distinguishes present spiritual benefits from the future end of physical death and discusses glorified life without affirming every speculative suggestion raised by participants. He explains “second coming” as a term whose scope must be understood in context, rather than simply counting separate movements. Several larger questions are reserved for later study. The concluding emphasis is practical: the brevity of present life and the hope of eternity should loosen attachment to possessions and strengthen present service and gospel witness.

questions.question: How does the opening review lead towards the new earth?
questions.answer: Saad compares earlier biblical eras with later fulfilment, placing the cross at the centre and moving through the millennial kingdom to the new heavens and new earth. He distinguishes the initial garden’s untested perfection from the secure future he describes through Christ. This establishes the transition to the next major section of the studies.

questions.question: What purposes does he give for the millennial kingdom?
questions.answer: Saad connects it with the fulfilment of promises to Abraham and Israel, the exposure of human sin even when Satan is restrained, and the bringing of Christ’s enemies under his feet. The kingdom is therefore not an unexplained pause in his sequence. These are the purposes presented within the premillennial reading taught in the course.

questions.question: What interpretive principle does Saad emphasise in comparing views?
questions.answer: He argues that figures, types and spiritual applications should not cancel the plain sense of promises to Israel. His distinction concerns how those promises relate to the church and future fulfilment. His focus is the continuing fulfilment of those promises alongside any spiritual application that the text itself gives.

questions.question: Why does he defend a rapture before the tribulation?
questions.answer: Saad identifies the period he calls the day of the Lord with seven years and says the church is promised exemption from it. That is his stated reason for rejecting a rapture in the middle or at the end of that period. During the explanation, he corrects his wording from the Lord’s Day to the day of the Lord.

questions.question: How does he distinguish Christ’s victory over death from death’s final removal?
questions.answer: Saad distinguishes the present opening of life with God through Christ from the future end of physical death’s power. He treats the later judgment and removal of death as the completion of the sequence being reviewed. The discussion does not imply that believers already avoid physical death in the present age.

questions.question: What roles are assigned to angels in the end-times discussion?
questions.answer: Saad describes angels proclaiming the gospel, carrying out judgments and gathering the elect at Christ’s coming. In the framework he teaches, that gathering is distinguished from the earlier rapture. The question about their role in the eternal state is expressly set aside for later attention.

questions.question: What is affirmed about glorified bodies, and what remains uncertain?
questions.answer: The discussion affirms embodied enjoyment of God’s presence and relates future resurrection life to Christ’s risen body. Saad does not confirm the audience’s suggestion about teleportation. He also declines to develop the proposed distinction between a rapture body and an eternal-state body in this review.

questions.question: Who does Saad identify with the abomination of desolation?
questions.answer: He identifies the Antichrist and explicitly frames his answer in terms of a person rather than only an event or object. He points to Daniel as background for the later Revelation discussion. His brief answer reports the interpretation used in this course, without adding a detailed identification beyond the source.

questions.question: How does he answer the objection that his sequence creates a third coming?
questions.answer: Saad treats second coming as a contextual theological term that can describe a period and its culmination, rather than merely counting separate arrivals. He compares this with the way first coming includes more than the moment of incarnation. In his explanation, the rapture and the later arrival on earth can belong within that broader usage.

questions.question: How should the teaching affect present life?
questions.answer: Saad urges listeners to consider eternity when facing present trials and making daily decisions. He calls for a looser hold on possessions and a stronger commitment to serving the Lord and sharing the gospel. The purpose of the review is therefore practical hope and faithfulness, not simply mastery of a prophetic timetable.
